chunks: And Zurārah said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:
“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said one day to ʿAmmār during a journey of his: ‘O ʿAmmār, it has reached us that you became junub. So what did you do?’”
He said: “I rolled in the dust, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”
He said: So he said to him: “That is how a donkey rolls. Why did you not do like this instead?”
Then he lowered his hands to the ground and placed them upon the earth, then wiped his forehead with his fingers and his two palms, one with the other, then he did not repeat that.

key_terms.أَجْنَبْتَ: You entered the state of janābah, requiring ritual purification.
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: Dust or soil, mentioned as what ʿAmmār rolled in.
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: The earth’s surface or clean ground used for tayammum.
key_terms.الْحِمَارُ: The donkey; used in the Prophet’s comparison to reject rolling in dust.
key_terms.جَبِينَيْهِ: His forehead, which was wiped in the demonstration.
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: His two palms or hands, wiped as part of tayammum.

ai.seo_question: How did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله teach tayammum to ʿAmmār?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of tayammum taught by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to ʿAmmār when he had become junub during travel. It shows that tayammum is performed by striking or placing the hands on the earth and wiping, rather than covering oneself in dust, and it serves as a practical Sunnah instruction in ritual purity.
